cohort: The study included 53,649 singleton pregnancies that booked and delivered at a large tertiary obstetric and neonatal unit, consisting of 139 (0.3%) extreme preterm deliveries between 24(+0) and 27(+6) weeks and 47,006 (99.7%) term deliveries (>=37 weeks).
finding: In pregnancies with extreme preterm delivery between 24(+0) and 27(+6) weeks, caesarean delivery and female neonates are associated with a lower incidence of neurological morbidity, and gestational age at delivery is the only significant factor in the prediction of intact perinatal survival.
mod_finding: Caesarean compared to vaginal delivery is associated with a lower incidence of neurological morbidity (6.1% vs. 19.3%; p = 0.016).
gest_age: 24(+0) to 27(+6) weeks for preterm deliveries; >=37 weeks for term deliveries
